title: The first peoples: a continent before Europe
goal: I can say what had already happened by 1492, using the past perfect.

sections.title: Welcome to Latin America
body: This is a 36-unit track on the history of Latin America, from the peoples who lived here long before 1492 to the end of the twentieth century: conquest and colonial life, independence and the new republics, revolution, dictatorship, and the return of democracy.

Every lesson is built around a short text in Spanish about a real period or episode. The words you need come from that text, and so does one grammar point you already know from earlier units, now practised on history. Screens and instructions are in English; the texts and the exercises are in Spanish. Each unit has five lessons and a consolidation lesson.
This track teaches no new grammar. It assumes you have finished A1 and A2 and the first 36 units of B1, and every word you learn here goes into the same review deck.
Let us begin before Europe arrived.

items: Say what had already happened by 1492, using the past perfect.
Say how the first peoples reached the Americas.
Say where maize and the potato were first grown.
Explain why nobody knows how many people lived in the Americas in 1492.
I can say what had already happened by 1492, using the past perfect.
I can say how the first peoples reached the Americas.
I can say where maize and the potato were first grown.
I can explain why nobody knows how many people lived in the Americas in 1492.
